issue: In a prolonged immigration detention bond hearing under 8 U.S.C. § 1226(a), must the government bear the burden of proof on dangerousness and flight risk, or may the noncitizen bear the burden at first?

sides.position: Due process requires the government to bear the burden of proof at a bond hearing, so the burden must always lie with the government (as held by the majority here).
cases: Hernandez Lara v. Lyons, 10 F.4th 19 (1st Cir. 2021)

sides.position: The burden may lie initially with the noncitizen at a bond hearing, shifting to the government only once detention becomes unreasonable.
cases: German Santos v. Warden Pike County Correctional Facility, 965 F.3d 203 (3d Cir. 2020)
Velasco Lopez v. Decker, 978 F.3d 842 (2d Cir. 2020)

this_court: The First Circuit holds that the burden must always lie with the government at the bond hearing.
quote: Further review of the majority's holding is warranted to resolve this circuit split and to bring the First Circuit back into compliance with controlling precedent.
cite: Hernandez Lara v. Lyons, 10 F.4th 19 (1st Cir. 2021)
